common_name: Prickly-Pear Opuntia Cactophilic Fly (Wing Length & Thorax Allometric Plasticity)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila buzzatii (2.9 µm, detail scale)

boundary_conditions: Periodic on a square pupal-cuticle patch (Turing's ring, extended to a 2-torus). No-flux is not used: the patch is a repeating detail window, not a whole-wing domain.

equations.kinetics: Schnakenberg 1979: f = a - u + u^2 v, g = b - u^2 v
equations.pde: du/dt = gamma f + D_u lap u; dv/dt = gamma g + D_v lap v
equations.critical_wavenumber: k_c^2 = gamma (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v)
turing_conditions: (D_v f_u + D_u g_v)^2 > 4 D_u D_v det(J)

parameters.note: Not the slot-2991 coefficients alpha_scale=1.405, beta_offset=0.284. Those belong to the 102 µm power-law stub.

reported_in_source: Norry, Vilardi & Hasson 1997 (Heredity 79:575): in D. buzzatii, correlations among size-related traits are rearranged by chromosome inversions in an adaptive polymorphism.
Norry, Vilardi & Hasson 1997 (Genetica 101:131): wing and thorax size traits have genetic and phenotypic correlations, with heritability that differs between body parts.

Cortese, Norry, Piccinali & Hasson 2002 (Evolution 56:2541): artificial selection on developmental time and wing length produces direct and correlated responses; the two traits are positively correlated.
Turing 1952: a homogeneous morphogen field can be unstable at a finite critical wavenumber k_c.
Schnakenberg 1979: the two-species kinetics f = a - u + u^2 v, g = b - u^2 v.
reconstructed_in_script: gamma is solved so the Schnakenberg critical wavelength on this Jacobian equals 2.908 µm.
A 16-wavelength periodic patch (46.528 µm) is integrated explicitly; the linear discrete dispersion peak is compared with the closed-form lambda across a gamma sweep.
Equal diffusion (D_u = D_v) is the negative control and must have max Re(sigma) < 0.
Mode count on a representative 1.70 mm wing chord is N = L / lambda. Allometry changes N, not lambda_c.
does_not_claim: That Norry or Cortese measured a 2.9 µm Turing wavelength.
That the species-card image is a wing or abdominal micrograph.
That D. bipectinata and D. cyrtoloma wavelengths were re-fit in this script; they are the predecessor (85.92 µm) and successor (207.6 µm) registry scales used only as the chronoseries contrast.
That the modulated species card is a pixel-level photograph of micro-ocelli.

specimen_image.license_note: Repository species-card fallback. Commons, iNaturalist, and GBIF had no CC bitmap of a live D. buzzatii adult on 2026-10-27.
